newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth to close all U.S. 5-and-10 stores - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth to close all U.S. 5-and-10 stores - WSJ.

text.p: Woolworth Corp. is expected to close all its F.W. Woolworth five-and-dime stores in the United States and record an after-tax charge of about $200 million to pay for associated costs, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the paper said the announcement that the more than 400 stores would be closed was expected on Thursday.

The article said the decision by the retail giant ended a long attempt to squeeze profits from a business that accounts for more than $1 billion of the company's annual sales, which exceed $8 billion.
The move also ends an effort to bring the 117-year-old business into retailing's modern age, the story said.
Last year the U.S. Woolworth stores reported an operating loss of $37 million, and the losses have worsened this year, according to analysts' estimates, the story said.
It is not clear what will happen to the more than 9,000 full- and part-time employees in the Woolworth division, the article said.
A Woolworth representative declined to comment, the story said.
The Journal said its information came from people familiar with the plans.
